_notes: Dense hybrid (qwen35: 32 blocks, full attention every 4th = 8 KV layers, 24 Gated-DeltaNet layers). GPU-first: every tensor on CUDA except token_embd (always host, mmap rows) and the FFN up/gate/down of layers 0-17 (--override-tensor), so all attention, recurrent state and KV stay on the GPU.

Fit estimate (3 Nov, from the pinned GGUF header, not measured): q8_0 KV at 65536 = 8 layers x 136 MiB = 1088 MiB; recurrent state ~50 MiB; CUDA compute buffer assumed 450 MiB (Qwen3.6 u128 64K measured 262-566 MiB in lab logs); CUDA context/cuBLAS assumed 300 MiB. Replace with the load log's numbers.

Working-set cap: an uncapped mmap load keeps GPU-uploaded pages in the working set (Groot uncapped 3 Nov: working set 4.69 GiB and available RAM 5.25 -> 0.99 GiB within 8 s of load). A dense model's CPU hot set is fixed (the CPU FFN bytes, read once per token), so the cap sits ~0.6 GiB above it and should trim only cold GPU-upload pages, unlike Groot's routed-expert churn. If soft faults climb during decode, raise the cap (and the RAM gate) rather than removing it.

Stop floors 2.5 GiB RAM / 1.0 GiB commit = the lab.check_stop_floors minimum (the requested 2.0 is refused by lab.py since 3 Nov). load_min_ram_free_gib = cap + reserve so the cap is never squeezed below the hot set; load_min_vram_free_mib = GPU estimate + 400 MiB stop floor (rounded up).

Thinking: the embedded template opens <think> only when enable_thinking is true (undefined = empty think block = non-thinking), so template_kwargs must carry it. preserve_thinking is NOT referenced by this template (accepted and ignored); reasoning before the last user query is always dropped by the template, so --reasoning-preserve only matters inside the current tool loop.
